changes: All four isolated platform/database harnesses wait for PostgreSQL at 127.0.0.1 over TCP, including the shell runner's final readiness assertion.
The official image's temporary initialization server listens only on a Unix socket, so a default pg_isready can succeed before that server shuts down and the final listener starts.
Production application behavior, migrations and configured databases are unchanged.
checks: The three controlled delayed-init cases accept Unix sockets after 0.68–0.79 seconds while TCP readiness returns exit 2, then accept TCP and execute SELECT 1 after 3.95–3.97 seconds.

The production Next.js build passes. Both corrected access-suite runs pass existing-device migration, fresh deployment, owner constraints, concurrent discovery history, live-only inventory, outage handling, user isolation, shared organization access, nonmember denial, mutation origin and watch-token scoping.
Changed scripts pass Prettier; the shell harness passes bash syntax validation. All owned PostgreSQL containers are removed.
scope: Real Next.js routes and PostgreSQL are used; upstream GitHub/engine HTTP is substituted in these access tests. Actual OAuth/SSO and browser playback are outside this route check.

A separate controlled readiness fixture is diagnostic evidence, not another application or production database. Its two shell-fixture setup failures are retained; the final SQL fixture avoids executing from the bind mount.
